items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The change is small and clear. `if queryset.query.is_sliced: raise ValueError("Prefetch querysets cannot use slices.")` uses the same nesting and message style as the existing raw()/values() check.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Structurally clean: a guard added to Prefetch.__init__. But it ignores the convention of adding a shared helper in related_descriptors.py and instead puts a permanent restriction in query.py, which blocks the feature the issue asks for.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: It validates at the boundary and fails early with a ValueError, so no error is swallowed. But it rejects a valid use case instead of handling it, and all 4 F2P tests fail (PrefetchLimitTests).

items.name: Per-parent slice semantics for open/bounded slices
items.name_zh: 开放/有界切片按父对象分区
items.evidence: No per-parent slicing at all: no Window/RowNumber partitioning and no clear_limits. Sliced Prefetch querysets now raise "Prefetch querysets cannot use slices.", so neither qs[n:] nor qs[n:m] is supported. F2P 0/4.
